title: Conduit performance portrait and cost-tier tiles specs
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design a compact, glancable 'Conduit' performance portrait for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route latency, throughput, token metrics and cost tiers in a single, vertically stacked tile. The portrait should be optimized for fast comparisons across routes, support canary/rollout annotations, and include drill-throughs to full trace views. This ticket captures the visual spec, interactions, chart choices, accessibility constraints, and handoff artifacts for engineering and analytics. Scope covers dashboard tile UX, responsive behavior for narrow sidebars, and an optional expanded modal with microtraces. Out of scope: backend telemetry changes, new telemetry collection (those are tracked in ENG-21459).
acceptance_criteria: Tile displays P50/P90/P99 latency ribbons and P50/P95 token cost per request for each route
Throughput sparkline (1m/5m/1h) with overlayed peak markers is present
Cost tier banding shown (free/standard/priority) with color legend and hover tooltip breakdown
Canary/rollout state visualized as a miniature traffic-split donut and annotated on latency ribbon
Clicking the tile expands to detailed modal with token waterfall and KV cache hit rate microchart
ARIA roles provided for primary metrics and keyboard navigation supports focus + Enter to expand
Design handoff includes Figma frames, token specs, and a brief CSS variable guidance doc
design_notes: Primary layout: left column route label + traffic weight badge; center column stacked ribbons (latency percentiles) with mini-sparklines on top; right column numeric summary (TPS, avg tokens, cost/request)
Latency ribbons: area-coded P50 (thin), P90 (thicker), and P99 (outline) to convey distribution without clutter; use patterned hatch for P99 in high-contrast mode
Throughput: small sparkline under latency with muted color and peak circles; default aggregation 5m with 1m hover resolution
Token flow mini: microbars representing input vs output tokens that scale logarithmically to avoid dominance by long prompts
Cost-tiering: use three discrete bands with semantic colors (green/yellow/purple) and an explanatory tooltip that maps to pricing buckets; also show estimated $/1000 reqs
Canary annotations: small pill marker on time-axis with hover revealing rollout ID, weight %, and start/end timestamps; clicking navigates to rollout detail panel
Expanded modal: left-side timeline with mini-traces, right-side token waterfall, bottom area for recent anomalous traces filtered by metric
Responsive: on narrow widths collapse numeric summary into an overflow menu and stack the ribbons vertically; preserve tap targets >= 44px
Performance: prefer canvas-rendered sparklines for large tile grids; fallback to SVG for accessibility readers
Colors: follow console token palette; ensure WCAG AA for text and 4.5:1 for critical data labels
decisions: Use percentile ribbons instead of multiple separate line charts to reduce vertical space
Prefer a single compact tile that can be repeated in grid for route-overview rather than separate charts per metric
Show cost estimate derived from token histogram rather than per-token raw price to simplify UX
Defer introducing new telemetry fields; rely on existing P95/P99 latency and token histograms from metrics pipeline
Accessibility first: include high-contrast patterns and screen-reader text blocks explaining each data element
